verdict.rationale: Cal.com does not document region or residency selection for its hosted service. Its own self-hostable MIT edition (Cal.diy) is aimed at users who want "full control over their scheduling infrastructure," and a self-hoster confirms running both the API and the database on their own infrastructure, which lets a user decide where data lives. That route has real limits: community reports say self-hosting is hard, public Docker images are being dropped, Cal.diy is positioned as personal/non-production use, and it lacks teams and orgs. Missing for 10: a documented region/residency choice on hosted Cal.com, a production-supported self-hosted path with enterprise features, and official residency documentation.
